title: An isomorphism on completed stalks implies etaleness near the point
statement: Let $f:Z\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $T$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $z\in Z$, set $t=f(z)$, and write $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{T,t}$ and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Z,z}$ for the completions of the local rings at their maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Suppose that the homomorphism $\widehat f_z^{\sharp}:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{T,t}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Z,z}$ induced by the actual stalk map $f_z^{\sharp}$ is an isomorphism. Then there is an open subscheme $W\subseteq Z$ containing $z$ such that $f|_W:W\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and the map $\kappa(t)\to\kappa(z)$ induced by $f$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0CAV, lemma-isomorphism-approximation, proof, first paragraph: an isomorphism on completed stalks implies smoothness by Tag 02HX (lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point), unramifiedness, and hence etaleness by Morphisms Tag 02GK (lemma-etale-smooth-unramified).

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ and $\varphi=f_z^\sharp$. By [lem-trf-smooth-stalk-artinian-criterion] these are nonzero Noetherian local rings; $\varphi$ is local because $f$ is a morphism of locally ringed spaces [def-pc-scheme]. The given completed map is the coordinatewise map induced by $\varphi$. Apply [lem-trf-completion-isomorphism-local-invariants]: $\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)B=\mathfrak m_B$ and the actual residue map $\kappa(t)\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism. This proves the residue-field conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, lemma-isomorphism-approximation, first proof paragraph: completed local invariants.

proof.text: For every small extension $q:C'\twoheadrightarrow C$ and compatible local maps $a:A\to C'$, $b:B\to C$ with $qa=b\varphi$, [lem-trf-completion-isomorphism-artinian-lifts] supplies a local $c:B\to C'$ with $qc=b$ and $c\varphi=a$. Its hypotheses hold because $A,B$ are Noetherian local, the given completed map is invertible, and the test rings are Artinian local. Thus the lifting condition in [lem-trf-smooth-stalk-artinian-criterion] holds. Since $f$ is locally of finite type and $T$ locally Noetherian, that criterion gives an open $U\ni z$ on which $f$ is smooth.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, first proof paragraph, invoking Tag 02HX (lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-unramified-maximal-ideal-residue-criterion] to $f|_U:U\to T$ at $z$. Restricting to an open subscheme leaves the local ring and the stalk map at a point unchanged; the restriction is locally of finite type by the affine-cover definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Step 1 gives the required maximal-ideal equality and a residue extension of degree one, hence finite separable (every element has a linear minimal polynomial). We obtain an open $W\subseteq U$ containing $z$ with $f|_W$ unramified. By [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], $f|_W$ is smooth. By [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] it is flat and locally of finite presentation; together with unramifiedness this is precisely etaleness by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Since $W$ is open in $U$ and $U$ is open in $Z$, it is the required open subscheme of $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, first proof paragraph; Morphisms Tags 02GF (lemma-unramified-at-point) and 02GK (lemma-etale-smooth-unramified).

split_report.summary: Q139 repair of the 5841-character returned proof: extracted three independent statement-only tasks of comparable argument size. The local invariants task carries old steps 2-3, the Artinian lift task old steps 5-6 and locality from 7, and the stalk/scheme criterion task old steps 1, 4 and the remaining part of 7. The parent keeps the original final etale-neighbourhood assembly and its statement unchanged. The full returned argument and its allocation are retained in report.md. Landing-return repair: compared the retained returned node with the current DAG (identical), reread all current cited statements and preserved valid citations, and distinguished both ring tasks from the newly present completed-base affine etale-span node. The delivery tool rebases this retained extraction onto the current live head. Revalidated the landing return on 2026-10-23 against current DAG and the server dry-run base 6be3c1a0822: the retained returned item is identical to the current item, all existing cited statements were reread, and no dependency replacement is needed. Made nonzero stalks and locality of the actual stalk homomorphism explicit in assembly step 1, citing the scheme definition. Updated the blueprint comparison to the latest snapshot 7284bb09daf97437d544c51882b325f9c52cd345.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the historical nodal-model/completion-approximation branch recorded in blueprint.from: specifically the first paragraph of Tag 0CAV used below lem-trf-isomorphism-completion-approximation. Current latest blueprint (main-20261023-1620, 7284bb09daf97437d544c51882b325f9c52cd345) lem-trf-local-term-locality uses the contracting-correspondence route and no longer spells out this historical auxiliary branch; no unit route or ancestor metadata is changed.

tool_uses.why: Only the implication smooth implies flat and locally finitely presented is used to conclude etaleness; this is a general morphism criterion, not a replacement of a unit step.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q139-b0dd7286d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Fourth delivery of the 2026-10-21 re-split; the repair note is released at stage 1. Live and side-live still have the old 8-step proof (5841 chars), so this head is not superseded. The three new nodes are byte-identical to the earlier heads 7732a9f9 and 4120ab14. Earlier heads were FIXed because item step 1 never showed that phi=f_z^sharp is local; the author has now added that argument. It cites def-pc-scheme, whose Stacks 01IJ (schemes.tex l.1660) says a morphism of schemes is a morphism of locally ringed spaces. That citation is enough, so no fix file is needed. The item statement is unchanged. Re-split check: old steps 2-3 became local-invariants; old 5-6 and the locality part of 7 became artinian-lifts; old 1, 4 and the scheme part of 7 became smooth-stalk-artinian-criterion; old 8 is item step 3. Nothing was dropped. The new statements are 1.2-1.5k chars each, and the item is a 3-step assembly of about 1.9k chars. I checked all three statements myself. local-invariants: h maps the maximal ideal and its powers onto those of the target, ker pi_n = m^n completed (adic-completion-mod-power), so every phi_n is an iso, and Nakayama gives phi(m_A)B=m_B. Tested on the identity, fields, Z_(p)->Z_p, and t->t^2 (consistent). artinian-lifts: both maps factor through finite quotients; q a_hat = b_hat h because the completion = i_A(A) + (m_A completed)^n; c is local because q is a surjection of nonzero local rings. stalk-criterion: this is 02HX (3)=>(1) (more-morphisms.tex 3575-3615) moved to stalk maps; the small-extension definition is length 1. Item step 3: unramified-maximal-ideal-residue (ii)=>(i), then open-immersion smooth composition, then sbc-lem-smooth-criterion (flat + locally of finite presentation), then def-weil-etale-morphism. This follows the 0CAV first proof paragraph (l.11097-11108). No SGA is cited. Duplicate candidates checked, including the nodes new on 10-23: lem-sfb-smooth-fixed-residue-artinian-test (scheme diagrams with fixed residue field, no local-map comparison; a possible future tool, not a duplicate), lem-sfb-scheme-artinian-smoothness-finite-type-tests (global smoothness), lem-sfb-ring-deformation-smoothness-test, smooth-artinian-lifting-at-point, local-completion-local-ring, flat-local-completion-iso (converse direction), isomorphism-completion-approximation, completed-base-affine-etale-span. Accepted tool use: sbc-lem-smooth-criterion.

lean.statement: theorem completedStalk_isomorphism_etale {Z T : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsLocallyNoetherian T] (z : Z) (h : IsIso (CommRingCat.ofHom (completedStalkMap f z))) : ∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ Etale (W.ι ≫ f) ∧ IsIso (f.residueFieldMap z)
